records.issue_text: **`app/models/topic_embed.rb#absolutize_urls`**: only rewrites `href`/`src` that start with `/`; it does not strip or validate dangerous schemes (`javascript:`, `data:`) on `a[href]`/`img[src]`. `import_remote` passes `attributes: %w[href src]` to Readability, which whitelists the attribute *names* but not their *values*, so a crafted source page/feed item containing `<a href="javascript:alert(1)">` will be imported and rendered verbatim (`cook_method: raw_html` skips the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline entirely — `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged). This is stored XSS served to every viewer of the embedded topic. Fix: sanitize/whitelist URL schemes (`http`/`https` only) when absolutizing, or route imported HTML through the standard sanitizer even in `raw_html` mode.

This silently removes existing functionality for anyone using this import task with categorized imports; it's also outside the stated scope ("embed URL handling and validation"). If intentional, it should be called out explicitly (and ideally `TopicEmbed.import`/`import_remote` should accept an optional category) rather than being a side effect of the refactor.

records.issue_text: **`app/models/topic_embed.rb#import`**: `contents << "\n<hr>\n..."` mutates the caller-supplied string in place. Callers (`PollFeed#poll_feed`, `import_remote`) happen to pass fresh strings today, but this is a latent footgun if a caller reuses/caches a content string across calls. Prefer `contents = contents + "..."` or `+=`.

records.issue_text: **`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb#poll_feed` / `TopicEmbed#import_remote`**: `open(url)` (open-uri) has no timeout configured. A slow/unresponsive feed or remote host can hang the hourly `PollFeed` job (and the inline `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` call made synchronously from `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`) with no bound, tying up a Sidekiq worker. Consider `open(url, read_timeout: ..., open_timeout: ...)`.
